page: Amazon Web Services r5b.xlarge is a memory-optimized server configuration running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory consists of 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a generous 8 GB per virtual CPU ratio. The server configuration includes no local storage drives, requiring workloads to utilize remote block storage, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are provisioned on this instance.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward memory capacity rather than raw compute speed. Multi-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 2461.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3482.56, rank in the lower tier relative to modern cloud servers due to the dual-core physical allocation. The PassMark memory benchmark scored 2145.03 in the middle tier, with large-block memory read bandwidth achieving 26.41 GB/sec. The absence of local solid-state drives places primary input-output overhead onto external network storage across the 1 Gbps network connection.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the r5b.xlarge delivers substantial memory density per core without requiring investment in unused GPU capability or high compute density. However, compute-bound tasks and heavy decompression workflows encounter clear throughput limitations. This server type is best suited for memory-intensive operational workloads, including distributed in-memory data stores, Redis caching, relational databases, and backend services with high RAM requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture and the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage paired with a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. In synthetic benchmarks, the r5b.xlarge shows mid-range memory performance with lower-percentile multi-core CPU and compression metrics resulting from its two-core physical footprint. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the hardware configuration is cost-efficient for setups needing sizable memory footprints without excess compute overhead. It is well suited for in-memory caching platforms, mid-scale relational database engines, and memory-constrained enterprise applications.
